findings.summary: In the current 4.35 tree the canonical ArkLib/OracleReduction/Security/Basic.lean (upstream-pinned) defines knowledgeSoundness through knowledgeSoundnessWith. That game runs the extractor's OptionT layer with `.run` and keeps `extractedWitIn? : Option WitIn` in the observation. A `none` result therefore counts as bad whenever relOut holds, and a failed protocol run still counts as non-acceptance. Oracle, Proof and OracleProof knowledge soundness all delegate to this definition. ImplicationsCore.lean has retired the vacuity theorem `knowledgeSoundness_vacuous` and the unconditional rbr corollary; nothing in ArkLib, ProximityPrize or Research references them any more. Its header and the genuine rbr-to-knowledge transport docstrings were reworded honestly (comment-only change, already in tree from an earlier agent; the file is HELD-BY CONFLICT-7). The acceptance regression is `Verifier.id_not_knowledgeSoundness_empty_relIn` in ProximityPrize/Extensions/OracleReduction/Security/Basic.lean (uncommitted, added earlier; the file is HELD-BY CONFLICT-7). It proves the accept-all identity verifier with relIn = ∅ and relOut = univ is not knowledge sound at any error < 1 for any extractor, which covers the always-failing one. The identity-extractor proof (`Verifier.id_knowledgeSoundness`) is in the canonical file, and the genuine transport `rbrKnowledgeSoundness_implies_knowledgeSoundness_genuine_of_marginal` is in ImplicationsCore.lean.

`Proof.knowledgeSoundness` (Security/Basic.lean) and `Proof.rbrKnowledgeSoundness` (Security/RoundByRound.lean, line ~925) already take `Set (Statement × Witness)` upstream. In ArkLib/OracleReduction/FiatShamir/DuplexSponge/Basic.lean, `DuplexSpongeFS.NARG.straightlineKnowledgeSoundness` now takes `relation : Set (Statement × Witness)`, and `StraightlineExtractor` now uses output witness `Unit`, matching Proof's output (statement Bool, witness Unit). findings.summary: The defect is already gone at the source level. After the upstream consolidation, the canonical getSumcheckRoundPoly keeps variable 0 (original coordinate i) free and sums the remaining variables over D.drop(i+1). The verifier sums over D.points i, and projectToNextSumcheckPoly fixes variable 0, so all three consume coordinates in the same front-first order. The asymmetric counterexample (D0={0}, D1={1}, H=X0) is now accepted. Domain.lean and Structured/SingleRound.lean are pinned upstream files and were left untouched. To prove the heterogeneous semantics, I added three kernel-checked theorems to the downstream extension ProximityPrize/Extensions/ProofSystem/Sumcheck/Structured/SingleRound.lean, each using only the standard axioms: sum_getSumcheckRoundPoly (for any domain family D, the verifier's sum over D.points i equals the witness sum over (D.drop i).cube), sum_projectToNextSumcheckPoly (the next-round claim over (D.drop (i+1)).cube for any D), and the helper sum_eval_cons_cast_piFinset.

Lookahead.lean (not pinned): I made the prose honest. The docs now say LookaheadSequenceFamily is only an internal-antichain plus length-bound interface, not an exhaustive maximal family. I added LookaheadSequenceFamily.empty, a kernel-checked witness that the empty family always satisfies the interface. The scan is now described as an unproved refinement of the paper's algorithm, not a 'paper-faithful optimization', with the zero-budget, absent-chain, fork and repeated-state cases, and the choice to treat a capacity-preserving successor as an error, flagged as unverified. The capacity guard is now described as excluding single-step loops only, not cycles like a->b->a. The lookAhead return documentation now describes what the scan actually does. The matching Backtrack.lean changes (BacktrackSequenceFamily scope, multi-step cycles caught by vCap, linearScanBackwards costing O(N^2)) are deferred because B042 holds that file. The full scan-refinement theorem is still open proof work.

Confirmed against current source. In extractCandidate, at an exact fit with lpCur > 0, msgEndIdx = m_plus_1 - 1 = outputState.length, so the bound check on the output index fails and the function returns none before reaching the only success branch. The L_ptr double count is also present: sumMessageBlocksBefore already includes the last message before i, and lpCur adds it again. The fix is written but not applied because B042 holds Backtrack.lean. It compiles cleanly on a scratch copy with no new warnings and applies with git apply --check. The patch: (1) compares input block msgEndIdx with the predecessor output block msgEndIdx-1, matching the salt check's Ld-1 / Ld-2 convention, and drops the used chars msgSize - (lpCur-1)*R so a full last block leaves an empty tail; (2) sets L_ptr := Ld + (L_P_before - lpCur) + L_V_before; (3) documents the remaining unproved items: only the last message is parsed (consecutive messages unhandled), missing entries are zero-filled, and the Finset.toList ordering is unspecified.

findings.summary: The old `UniPoly.degree` actually returned the coefficient count (`natDegree + 1`). I renamed it to `trimmedSize` and gave it an honest docstring. The lemmas are renamed to `Trim.size_eq_trimmedSize` and `Trim.eq_trimmedSize_of_equiv`, and their callers in `eq_of_equiv` are updated. I added a real `degree : WithBot ℕ` (zero polynomial is ⊥) and a `natDegree` (zero polynomial is 0), matching Mathlib's conventions. New lemmas connect the three: `trimmedSize_eq_zero_iff_degree_eq_bot`, `trimmedSize_eq_natDegree_add_one`, `degree_eq_natDegree`. I also fixed the `degreeBound` docstring, which said 'size' when the definition returns the last index (size - 1). No consumers exist outside this file.

I moved division into its own `Division` section over `[Field F] [BEq F]`, which removes the old diamond between the section's `[Ring R]` and the `[Field R]` argument. `divModByMonicAux` now trims both inputs first and returns (0, p) when the divisor is zero. Its fuel is `p.trim.size + 1 - q.trim.size`, so equal-degree inputs get their cancellation step. Each step stops once the remainder is shorter than the divisor, and the quotient is trimmed. `div` and `mod` normalize with an R-scalar smul. `mod` now scales the normalized remainder back by `q.leadingCoeff`, and modulo zero returns `p` (trimmed). The section docstring now says plainly that no correctness theorem is proved. I added `#guard` regression checks over ℚ: #[1]/#[1] = (1, 0), an exact division, padded inputs, a constant divisor, `1 mod 2X = 1`, a non-monic divisor, and division by zero. The reconstruction and remainder-degree theorems the brief asks for are still not proved; the docstring says so.

I replaced the coefficient-copy stub with a real interpolation. A new `Lagrange.basis` builds each basis polynomial ∏_{j≠i}(X - ω^j)/(ω^i - ω^j). `interpolate` (now over `[Field F] [BEq F]`) returns the trimmed sum of `r i • basis i`. The docstring now states degree < n and the unchecked requirement that the nodes be distinct; when they are not, the output is meaningless. `#guard` checks over ℚ cover the brief's counterexample (values [1,1] at nodes 1 and 2 now give the constant 1), the identity function giving X, and evaluation reproducing the values at all 4 nodes for ω = 2. No formal evaluation theorem is proved; the docstring says so.

oc_g224_witness_exact.py now builds the actual additive cross-correlation X = Er*Om + Or*Em and checks <W,X> = eo+oe. The old separate-transform product is kept only as provenance (sepProd) and labelled as not a packet mode. findings.summary: Confirmed: `genRSC` (ProximityGen.lean) accepts any injective `exp : parℓ ↪ ℕ` and samples uniformly from the image set, while `mca_rsc` and `mca_johnson_bound_CONJECTURE` (MutualCorrAgreement.lean) quantified over that arbitrary exponent map. Both are refuted for exponents (0, q-1) (the F_7 counterexample). Fix: both named Props now start with the consecutive-exponent guard `(∀ j, exp j < Fintype.card parℓ_type) → ...`. Together with injectivity this forces the exponent set to be {0,…,ℓ-1}, and under that guard the image-uniform law equals sampling a uniform scalar (see GenSeam.hasMutualCorrAgreement_genRSC_iff_uniform). The docstrings record the counterexamples and the distribution caveat. The genRSC comment also gets a CAVEAT paragraph. Every other consumer delegates to these theorems with unchanged types and already assumes exp j = j. `mca_capacity_bound_CONJECTURE` is unchanged: it is already documented as trivially true.

Confirmed: the premises `hPG`/`hCA` of hasMutualCorrAgreement_of_proximityGap, mca_linearCode and mca_linearCode_udrFree range over all stacks with no badness restriction. Added the kernel-checked barrier theorem `one_le_errStar_of_allStack_proximityBound` (axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound). It shows the zero stack forces `1 ≤ errStar δ` on the whole admissible range. Rewrote the three docstrings: they no longer say 'REPAIRED/faithful repair/genuinely derived'. They now say these are conditional monotonicity wrappers whose premise no sub-unit proximity-gap bound can supply, not a CA→MCA derivation, and that the genuine bridge is still open. The module docstring now states the omitted-sign and normalization convention, notes that separable_iff_discr_eq_zero is unaffected, and tells consumers who want the conventional value to use Polynomial.discr.

findings.summary: Replaced the placeholder canonical initializer `new := fun _ => 0` in ArkLib/Data/Hash/DuplexSponge.lean with a specified IV-in-capacity packing `CanonicalSpongeState.ivToState`. It zeroes the rate and puts the IV into the capacity starting at R, chunk by chunk (`ivUnit`/`ivUnitBytes`), which is the spongefish Keccak `state[R..R+32] = iv` layout. The docstring states the limits of the packing: IV bytes that do not fit are dropped, and a chunk that fails to deserialize becomes 0. New lemmas: `new_eq_ivToState`, `ivToState_getElem_capacity`, `DuplexSponge.new_state`, `ivUnit_uint8`, and `ivToState_injective_uint8` (for UInt8 with 32 <= C). New regression `HashStateWithInstructions.new_ds_ne_of_generateTag_ne`: for the canonical UInt8 sponge with 32 <= C, two domain separators with different tags get different initial sponges, whatever their schedules. This regression is conditional on the tags differing; it does not compute two concrete Keccak tags in the kernel.

`FSVerifierState.fillNextUnits` now reads unit i from `extract (i*size) ((i+1)*size)` instead of passing the length as the end offset. New kernel-checked regressions (`decide +kernel`, no native_decide) in namespace FSStateRegression, using a toy LogSponge and a two-byte Unit16 unit: reading two UInt8 units, reading two Unit16 units, rejecting a truncated 3-byte transcript, prover serialization, multi-unit prover/verifier round trips for UInt8 and Unit16, and a hint round trip.

deferred_edits.edit:
(L74) Module header lines ~23-39 and ~75-78: replace the claim that the genuine betaRec weight 'grows linearly and unboundedly in t' / 'increases without bound' and that 'there is no matchingSet' satisfying hcard with: the proven L10 bound weight(betaRec t) <= (2t+1)*d*D is only an UPPER bound that grows in t; it gives no lower bound on the actual weight (cancellation is possible; e.g. Bcoeff = 0 gives betaRec (t+1) = 0 for all t, see the regression lemma below), so it does not show the infinite-range hcard is unsatisfiable for genuine families. What is true is that the infinite-range hcard cannot be DISCHARGED from the linear upper bound plus a fixed finite matchingSet (the sufficient budget (2t+1)dD*d_H eventually exceeds any fixed card); the finite-range counting interface is the honest replacement for that discharge route. Replace 'with the corrected interface, hcard is **satisfiable**' with 'the finite-range concrete budget can be met by a single bound at T'. Step 5 docstring (~306-319): delete 'strictly more honest', 'The converse fails — that is precisely the F5 finding', and 'Demonstrates the corrected interface asks for strictly less'; replace with 'This only proves the implication old bundle -> finite bundle; no converse failure (strict weakness) is formalized here.' Also note at curveCoeffPolys_of_section5DataFin (~255-283) that its final representative argument does not use htrunc (L13). Rename '(satisfiable)' wording at ~223 and ~262/295 to 'finite-range'. Add regression (verified to compile, standard axioms):

/-- Audit L74 regression: the generic `betaRec` interface admits cancellation — with the zero numerator family every successor value vanishes, so the growing upper weight budget is not a lower bound on the actual weight. -/
theorem betaRec_succ_of_zero_coeff (x₀ : F) (R : F[X][X][Y]) (H : F[X][Y]) [Fact (Irreducible H)] [Fact (0 < H.natDegree)] (hHyp : Hypotheses x₀ R H) (t : ℕ) :
    ArkLib.betaRec x₀ R H hHyp (fun _ {_} _ => (0 : 𝒪 H)) (t + 1) = 0 := by
  rw [ArkLib.betaRec_succ]
  refine Finset.sum_eq_zero fun _ _ => Finset.sum_eq_zero fun _ _ => ?_
  split_ifs
  · rfl
  · ring

(plus `#print axioms ArkLib.HcardDischarge.betaRec_succ_of_zero_coeff` in the axiom-audit block; adjust variable binders to the file's `variable {F}` setup).

(L74) Add before betaCurveInput_of_section5 the arithmetic impossibility lemma (verified to compile, standard axioms):

/-- Audit L74: the infinite-range concrete budget `hcardConcrete` is uninhabitable whenever all three factors are ≥ 1 (take `t = max k n`). -/
theorem not_forall_card_gt_linear (n k a b c : ℕ) (ha : 1 ≤ a) (hb : 1 ≤ b) (hc : 1 ≤ c) :
    ¬ ∀ t, k ≤ t → (n : WithBot ℕ) > (((2 * t + 1) * a * b * c : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ) := by
  intro h
  have h1 := h (max k n) (le_max_left _ _)
  have h1' : (2 * max k n + 1) * a * b * c < n := WithBot.coe_lt_coe.mp h1
  have h2 : n ≤ (2 * max k n + 1) * a * b * c := by
    have : n ≤ 2 * max k n + 1 := by omega
    have h3 : 2 * max k n + 1 ≤ (2 * max k n + 1) * a * b * c := by
      have := Nat.mul_le_mul (Nat.mul_le_mul (Nat.mul_le_mul (le_refl (2 * max k n + 1)) ha) hb) hc
      simpa only [Nat.mul_one] using this
    omega
  omega

and a corollary `not_hcardConcrete (hd1 : 1 ≤ R.natDegree) (hH : 0 < H.natDegree) (hdH_D : H.natDegree ≤ D) : ¬ ∀ t, k ≤ t → (↑matchingSet.card : WithBot ℕ) > (((2 * t + 1) * R.natDegree * D * H.natDegree : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ) := not_forall_card_gt_linear _ _ _ _ _ hd1 (by omega) hH`. Then in the betaCurveInput_of_section5 docstring (~354) state: 'Under hd1/hH/hdH_D the hypothesis hcardConcrete is uninhabitable (not_hcardConcrete), so this builder is vacuous; use betaCurveInputFin_of_section5. This is a fact about the concrete sufficient budget, not about the actual betaRec weights.'

It proves the point the finding makes: the unrestricted assumptions fail. Specifically: (1) exhaustiveDlog plus exhaustive-search t-SDH and ARSDH adversaries that win with probability 1 (tSdhExperiment_exhaustiveAdversary_eq_one when g2 != 1; tSdhExperiment_trivialGenerator_eq_one when g1 = 1; arsdhExperiment_exhaustiveAdversary_eq_one when g1, g2 != 1 and p >= D+2). (2) not_tSdhAssumption_of_lt_one and not_arsdhAssumption_of_lt_one: the unrestricted assumptions are false for every error < 1 in the nondegenerate setting. (3) Adversary-class-indexed assumptions tSdhAssumptionFor and arsdhAssumptionFor, with *_iff_univ bridges to the originals, antitone .mono lemmas, and tSdhExhaustiveAdversary_not_mem_of_assumptionFor. The module docstring says that conditional reductions remain logically valid but carry no computational guarantee under the unrestricted premise, that their usable content is the pointwise bound on the specific reduction adversary, and that a resource-bounded class closed under reductions is not formalized. findings.summary: PROVING.md now describes Assumptions.lean as a data-only registry that declares no axiom. Its layout table has the real directories (Core, Fleet, Games, Refund; no Zkpc/Theorems) and it states the actual CI limits. OPEN-PROOFS.md marks challenge-firing done (T4Fires.lean: challengeResp_flat_fires and challengeResp_flat_never_bot are in the proved table) and updates the CI ground rule. It also gains a 'Known gaps between the statements and the claims' section that keeps the SM01-SM09 bridges open and notes the historical K3/K4 overclaims. DELIVERY.md: 12pp corrected to 14pp, the 'axiomatized' wording replaced, T7 hypothesis described accurately, the axiom-clean build no longer read as implying refinement/deadline/wire results, K5 labelled historical. README.md and experiment-outcome.md claims are qualified the same way, and 'caught every attempt at drift' is narrowed to the recorded episodes. No obligation was relabelled complete apart from T4Fires, which really is proved.

CI: the raw greps are replaced by scripts/lean_token_scan.py, a lexical scan that strips nested block/doc/line comments and strings and checks code only. After lake build CI runs a new kernel gate, scripts/check-axioms.lean: a meta command that walks the transitive kernel dependencies of every declaration in a Zkpc.* module and fails on any axiom other than propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound (sorryAx and custom axioms included). Its log plus lean --version is uploaded as the axiom-gate-log artifact. Test status: the gate logic passed positive and negative tests on Lean 4.35 core (the negative test catches sorryAx and the lc* axioms). The scanner was tested on the real sources (clean) and on a synthetic bad tree (catches sorry and an out-of-file axiom, ignores docstrings and strings). Never compiled against Zkpc under its own v4.30.0 toolchain, which is not installed here, and its mathlib/VCV-io deps were not fetched.

The ZkpcFleetS2.cfg and ZkpcFleetS3.cfg header comments now match their actual constants. tla-findings.md now names ZkpcFlatLiveHonest.cfg and ZkpcFlatLiveByz.cfg instead of the absent ZkpcFlatLive.cfg. It labels all counts and traces as historical, states that tla/runs/*.log is git-ignored and absent, and adds a 'Reproducing these runs' section: exact TLC commands for every config, what must be recorded (TLC and Java versions), current SHA-256 hashes of all .tla/.cfg inputs, and the required ablation outcomes (NoBind must violate ExcessBound, NoMergeEv must violate ConflictSlashed, LiteralRev2 must violate PoolSolvency). No fresh TLC replay: tla2tools.jar is not on this machine, and downloading it needs user permission.

Spec.md section 5 assumption 5 now states fixed-plaintext re-randomization: for each plaintext m and each ciphertext decrypting to m, Rerand is distributed as a fresh Enc(pk,m), independent of the input's randomness given m. It says why independence from the plaintext is impossible and that plaintext hiding is the separate IND-CPA clause. The T4 statement now says B-rerand's perfect bound holds only in the ideal fresh-handle model and that the concrete reduction is the open full-wire bridge. The Assumptions.lean registry/table docstrings and the BInstances.lean module docstring were corrected to match. Lean edits are docstring-only; comment_only_check passed on both files.

Spec.md T3 anti-vacuity is narrowed: it shows the emission-based floor does not detect fresh-index retries (D=100, C=10, three emissions, refund 70 meets the floor) and says MC2's value needs a payer property indexed by logical authorizations. T7 anti-vacuity is corrected: one nonzero-digest observation leaves every k possible; slope reuse leaks k from two observations at distinct nonzero digests; a digest-0 signal is a confounder. Still to do: a Lean calibration of the two-observation, distinct-nonzero-digest experiment against fresh slopes (T7.lean, SM07 territory, not compilable here). It is listed as open in OPEN-PROOFS.md and in deferred_edits.

paper/refs.bib privatex402 author corrected to 'Conor McMenamin and Artem Grigor', matching the primary byline and the existing synthesis/verification notes. paper/paper.pdf is not regenerated (no LaTeX toolchain here); DELIVERY.md now says the PDF predates the correction and must be rebuilt and checked.

The RESEARCH.md TLDR no longer claims anonymity sets are 'always smaller' than the clientele. It now separates payment-unit sets (TumbleBit/A2L) from customer-unit sets (BOLT/zkChannels), states the justified non-strict bound (on distinct payers), notes the payment count can exceed the number of distinct clients, and keeps the abort and intersection caveats as conditional shrinkage. The archived hub-multihop-report.md 'you will not reach' claim was fixed the same way, with a marked audit-correction note in its banner.

It states that no refinement onto Core.Step exists, that the honest open'->spend->redeem->sweep trace pays nothing, and that conflicting tickets cannot be disputed through the tuple. It calls the tuple a typing exercise and lists what closing the gap needs. A real refinement or joint-state proof is new research-scale work and could not be compiled here (no v4.30.0 toolchain or deps).

Verified: T5_payer_close_liveness is existential, and Step.tick is always enabled. Core/T5.lean header and theorem docstrings now say this. They add a scope note: no trace or fairness predicate exists, weak fairness gives at most eventual settlement and never the exact t+tau clock, and extra ticks are always possible. 'Against any adversary scheduling' and 'every execution settles' were removed, and GATE-NOTE 1 now says the deadline is attainable, not enforced. A pathwise deadline would need a new scheduling rule plus proofs, which could not be compiled here.

Verified: forceClose is unguarded from every open state, including genesis. Refund/State.lean gains a GATE-NOTE saying the forfeit has no response window or cheater proof, so the layer is settlement-outcome arithmetic only. Refund/Safety.lean: the T3_B_floor header and docstring now say slashed=false is a premise. The reference to the nonexistent honest_close_not_slashed was removed. close_not_slashed is relabelled as one-step preservation, and the H5 race prose was narrowed. Adding a response window to the machine is a model change that cannot be compiled here.

Verified: flatSpend resamples nf_e per emission and ignores the epoch, and x=0 is allowed (M:=F, x:=m). In Games/FlatInstance.lean the 'each key queried once' argument is now limited to index keys. The x=0 exclusion claim is replaced by a statement that it is not encoded (citing rln_x_zero_degenerate). The epoch GATE-NOTE now states the 1 vs 1/|F| equality mismatch, that this is not a checked ROM marginal, and that no concrete-to-ideal reduction exists. Games/T4.lean's F2/F3 ledger and headline docstring were corrected the same way. A cached-pseudonym instance and a re-proved coupling are not doable unchecked.

Verified. Games/T7.lean now describes hobliv as a global distributional-independence assumption. It is not a good event, PPT or query bound, and it does not follow from 'no query hit k'. The GATE-NOTE now says the proposed (q_A+q_Id+q_E+1)/|F| bound is wrong for this game, gives the zero-digest attack with win probability 1-(1-1/p)^2 > 1/p, and drops the 'this IS the PPT scoping' claim. The T7_frame_bound docstring was renamed in prose to 'conditional blind-guess form'. The full query-accounting bound is open research.

Games/Unlink.lean zkBridgeObligation docstring now says it is open: only a definition, with no Sfull built or proved for any instance. Games/T4.lean has a scope note that the headline applies only to the proof-free ideal flatInstance. It also says 'discharged' means 'idealized away', and that dropping pi from a datatype is not a ZK proof. BInstances.lean is held by B113, and its O3 GATE-NOTE already discloses that serve accepts arbitrary receipts. The T4Fires witness exists, so no change was needed there.

Verified both items. (1) Games/T7.lean module and frameGameAReuse docstrings now say: the digest-0 point reveals k whatever the slope, so the witness does not isolate slope reuse; both games build evidence inside a game that holds k; and neither is a protocol calibration. (2) Games/Calibration.lean: the multTag section, header bullet and battery GATE-NOTE now say the q=1-safety claim is false for this interface. Adversary-chosen genesis counters (lastEpoch=some 0, epochCnt=1) give a one-ticket perfect distinguisher. The q=2 winner stays valid. New nonzero-digest calibration games and internally initialised counters are code changes that could not be checked under the missing toolchain.

findings.summary: docs/kb/deltastar-okamoto-syndromespace-adversarial-read-2026-06-13.md: the reversed inequality is corrected. '2(m+1)/3 > m-1' holds only for m<5, so on the band (1-rho)/3 < delta <= (1-rho)/2 disjoint supports actually satisfy the Thm 6.2 witness hypothesis. The disjoint-support argument now applies only inside the prize window (delta > 1-sqrt(rho) >= (1-rho)/2). The countermodel is relabelled as a proposed, unconstructed and unchecked probe target, and the claims that it 'machine-checks' anything or 'directly contradicts the abstract' are removed. The intro is softened to match.

docs/kb/deltastar-exact-asymptotic-formula-and-budget.md: added a statement that each row is a maximum over a different family of admissible far directions for each threshold s. This is why rows are not monotone (n=24,k=3 gives I(9)=16 < I(10)=19). s* now uses an explicit first-crossing rule, and the doc notes the crossing need not be unique. 'Decays' becomes 'trends down', and the plateau claim is corrected. The engine source is not in the tree, so the exact rule for which directions are admissible at each s could not be re-read.

kb doc and the module docstring of Research/ProximityPrize/Frontier/_SYZ6FinerGradingCeiling.lean: the 'B -> infinity, tends to 1/3 from above, unattained infimum' claim is replaced. On the fixed 2^30 domain the block count must be B=2^j with j<=30. The fixed-domain optimum was computed exactly: C=B/2-1 for even j and B/2-2 for odd j, minimum at B=2^30 with radius 357913941/2^30 = 1/3 - 1/(3*2^30), which is below 1/3. The arithmetic side conditions were checked at that point. The wrong 2^13 example is corrected (3 does not divide 2^13-(2^12-1); the true optimum there is 358088703/2^30). The doc notes that no Lean proof exists for gradings finer than 1024.

docs/kb/deltastar-466-r180-gaussian-tower-fixed-point-2026-07-08.md: states that the cancel and polar statistics depend only on the angle, so the 2/pi match tests only the angle law. The 'uniform angle preserves the R168 budget' target is replaced by an explanation of why a uniform angle alone cannot pay a normalized MGF budget (the radius r is unconstrained), plus a corrected three-part target: uniform angle, chi^2_2 radius, and radius-angle independence. The 'explains' claim is downgraded to a conditional, and the Gaussian hypothesis now requires i.i.d. centred Gaussians.

docs/kb/deltastar-466-r317-heavy-resonance-inverse-2026-07-09.md: added a != b to the resonance definition. Without it, the identity 1/1 qualifies at every prime and the inverse claim is vacuous. The census sentence, proof step 3 and the summation over pairs are updated to match.

docs/kb/collinearity-vs-count-CRUX-RESOLVED-2026-06-14.md: replaced the false claim that close codewords are 'collinear for elementary interpolation reasons'. Below the unique-decoding radius collinearity holds only vacuously, because at most one codeword is that close. From the interior onset (n-k+1)/(2n), below Johnson, the doc's own machine-built examples show non-collinear close triples, so collinearity is not forced.

docs/kb/Iinf-campaign/05-qindep-workflow-verdict.md and the module and theorem docstrings of Research/ProximityPrize/Frontier/_PIndependenceLangWeil.lean: the product of residuals vanishes at a satisfied point, not at agreement on every point. The roots of the product R_S are the union of the per-point roots, while the per-subset bad set is their common root set: at most one element, nonempty only if all gamma_z coincide. The p-independence 'brick' and the prize-scale = char-0 conclusion are marked not established, and the headline brick count is corrected. The Lean root-count theorems are kept as correct generic facts, with docstrings saying they do not prove that the incidence is independent of q.

docs/kb/deltastar-as-lacunary-polynomial-root-count.md: added the allowed-binomial counterexample. x^b(x^{n/2}-1) gives at least n/2 roots, e.g. x^12-x^4 has 8 > 7 roots at (16,4), with similar cases at (16,2) and (24,6).
